headline: Microsoft has set up a new group called Xbox Labs to explore decompiling and rebuilding games, the technique behind fan-made ports and mashups, many of them made with AI.
score_reason: Official statement from Xbox's chief executive relayed by The Verge; interesting for games and AI but with no product yet, so it stays at the curator's 5.
importance_line: Gamers and modders may get official tools and more ways to play old games on new devices, while publishers face open questions over who owns the results; The Verge says the open question is how Microsoft will treat unauthorized use of its games, and the group's actual output is not yet known.
summary: The Verge reports that Asha Sharma, chief executive of Microsoft's Xbox, has created Xbox Labs, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists that will experiment with decompiling games (turning finished games back into editable code) and rebuilding them to run on other devices, a practice modders are already pursuing, often with AI help. Sharma says the group will build in the open and share its tools with developers, while The Verge notes that Microsoft did not answer its question about unauthorized use of its games.
notes: Read in full. The Verge's opinion is attributed. Announcement date not stated in the article; pool time is 13 Oct 2026.
